question: On a real account, does a pin made the way a user makes one keep content that is then readable through a mount with the provider unreachable?
why_now: All five milestone 3 boxes now say the same thing and nothing else: no measured evidence on a real account. The feature was connected on 2026-09-10 and covered by nine tests including six through a kernel mount, but every one of them uses a fixture provider. A fixture cannot produce the shapes a real drive does -- content revisions that change block keys, a linked collection whose scope is not the account's own drive, files whose size the index and the provider disagree about.
workload: An isolated validation connection, disabled so no daemon mounts it, on the user's real business drive. A fixture folder is created and one generated file uploaded into it, so nothing pre-existing is touched. The file is pinned through the same request path the command line uses; the engine is then rebuilt on the same directory so the in-memory cache is empty; the mount is brought up; the provider is made unreachable by cancelling its token source; the file is read through the kernel.
endpoint: Whether the read succeeds, whether its bytes match what was uploaded, and whether any provider content request was made during it.

predictions.claim: The pin is accepted and reports resident bytes greater than zero through the engine's own status.
predictions.role: without this the rest measures an accounting entry

predictions.claim: After a rebuild and a mount, the file reads through the kernel with the provider unreachable, byte for byte.
predictions.role: the box's claim, on a real drive

predictions.claim: No provider content request is made during that read.
predictions.role: discriminator -- bytes fetched during the read would prove nothing about the pin

predictions.claim: An unpinned file in the same folder cannot be read under the same conditions.
predictions.role: discriminator -- without it a provider that quietly kept serving would look like a working pin

decision_rule: P1 through P4 all holding is what the five milestone 3 rows are missing and nothing more; each row also has clauses this does not address, and the ledger says which. If P4 fails the run is void, because the offline condition was never established.

safety.account: A separate validation connection with a write grant, disabled, in its own state directory. Not the user's working account and not mounted by any daemon.
safety.writes: One new folder and one generated file inside it. Nothing pre-existing is read, changed, moved or deleted.
safety.cleanup: The fixture folder is retained, as every validator here does. Removing it on a real tenant is a human decision.
